actions.description:
Executes the specified agent and returns a non-streaming JSON response with the complete agent output. The agent must be in active status and belong to the specified location. locationId is required in the request body. 

**Session Management:**
- For the first message in a new session, do not include the `executionId` in the request payload.
- The API will return an `executionId` along with the agent response, which uniquely identifies this conversation session.
- To continue the conversation within the same session, include the `executionId` from the previous response in subsequent requests. This allows the agent to maintain conversation context and history across multiple interactions.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Agent ID to execute (must be in active status and belong to the location)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Origin channel attributed to this execution for auditing (e.g. public_api, internal)

message.description: Message to send to the agent
message.example: How can you help me with my marketing?

executionId.description: Unique session identifier that maintains conversational context across multiple interactions within the same agent session. Omit this field for the first message in a new session. Include the executionId returned from the previous response to maintain context in subsequent messages.

inputVariables.description: Input variables to pass to the agent. These should match the input variables defined in the agent configuration.

versionId.description: Published version ID to execute. If not provided, the latest published production version will be used.

contactId.description: Contact ID to associate with this execution. When provided, contact data will be hydrated and made available to the agent.

actions.description: Runs one JSON turn against the published production snapshot. Omit sessionId on the first turn and pass the returned sessionId on subsequent turns. Reuse the same Idempotency-Key only when retrying the exact same logical turn. For a 429 response, retry that key only when retryable is true and Retry-After is present.

parameters.description: Unique key for this logical turn. Maximum 128 characters.

extraVariables.description: Optional JSON variables. Maximum encoded size is 32 KiB and maximum nesting depth is 5. Runtime identity names are reserved and rejected with 400: the roots `account`, `contact` and `location`, and the keys `agentId`, `agencyId`, `companyId`, `contactId`, `executionId`, `locationId`, `sessionId` and `userId`. Matching is case-insensitive and applies at the top level and under the optional `global`, `inputs`, `raw` and `runtime` prefixes, in either dotted (`runtime.contact.id`) or nested form. Use the endpoint `locationId` and the top-level `contactId` instead. These names nested under one of your own keys (for example `customer.contactId`) are accepted.

actions.summary: Answer every question of one form in a single write.
actions.description:
Records up to 12 answers in one run write and resumes the run once,
so a multi-question form does not resume the planner per answer.
Same per-answer rules as `POST …/answers` (records review approval
by `approve:<reviewId>` only, `decline:<reviewId>` declines,
anything else is a change request); `attachmentIds` are
ignored here. Project-scoped (`404` for another project's run);
`locationId` comes from the session, never from the body.

Idempotency: an answer whose `capId` and `correlationId` match the
recorded one is skipped; when every answer is such a duplicate
nothing is written and the run is not resumed again (still `202`).

answers.description: Each item is validated as `AnswerQuestionRequest`; `attachmentIds` are ignored on this route.

actions.description:
Idempotent on `planId`: a second (or concurrent) apply of the same plan
returns the first apply's result without writing again (`queued` while
the first is still running). Apply re-checks the stored change against
what exists now; when it moved, the answer is 409 `change_plan_stale`
with a fix (plan again). An expired plan is 409 too. A `partial` result
stays open: applying the same plan again finishes only what is left.
Another location's or project's plan is 404.

actions.summary: Read an app's stack and open its sandbox for editing.
actions.description: Returns the app's stack, which decides how its code is written, and its kernel bundle, and opens the app's sandbox: read and edit it once `sandbox.status` is `ready`. A `react_native_app_kernel_v1` app is a phone app: its screens are files under `apps/mobile/app-extensions/`, registered with `POST .../sandbox/extension-routes`. Every other stack is a web portal.

actions.summary: Save the app's sandbox files as the point it restarts from.
actions.description: Saves the sandbox's files so a sandbox that restarts comes back with them. Call it after a set of `POST .../sandbox/edit` calls and before starting the run that builds them: a sandbox that restarts in between otherwise comes back with the files as they were at the last save.

reason.description: `turn_complete` after a set of edits (the default); `build_passed` after a build that passed.

actions.summary: Write or delete one file in the app's sandbox.
actions.description: Writes or deletes one file in the app's sandbox. After a set of edits, save them with `POST .../sandbox/checkpoint`, then start a run with `externalAgent: true` to check, build and deploy them. A React Native app (`react_native_app_kernel_v1`) writes only under `apps/mobile/app-extensions/` and `apps/mobile/application-assets/`; its `routes.ts` is generated, so register its screens with `POST .../sandbox/extension-routes` instead of writing that file.

path.description: File to write or delete, relative to the workspace root.

content.description: The file's full new content, encoded as `encoding` says.

actions.summary: Register, rename or remove a React Native app's screens.
actions.description: Changes the screen list of a React Native app (`react_native_app_kernel_v1`) once its screen files are written with `POST .../sandbox/edit`: `app-extensions/routes.ts` is generated from these changes, never written as text. Send several changes as one `batch`: all of them apply or none does, and a resent batch that is already in effect changes nothing (a repeated single `add` is refused as `duplicate_id`). The run started next with `externalAgent: true` checks the screens, saves them as a mobile revision and deploys the preview.

action.description: One change, or several as `{ "action": "batch", "changes": [...] }`. A change is `{ "action": "add", "route": { "id", "label", "icon", "requires"?, "parent"?, "copyKey"?, "filledIcon"? } }`, `{ "action": "rename", "id", "newId", "label"? }` or `{ "action": "remove", "id" }`. `id` is kebab-case and names the screen file; `icon` is one of the kernel's icon names, and an unknown one is refused; `parent` makes the screen a detail pushed from that route.

actions.summary: Search the app's code for literal text.
actions.description: Finds where text appears in the app's source files (ts, tsx, js, jsx, vue, json, md, css), with dependencies and build output left out. The text is matched literally, not as a pattern. Read the files it finds with `POST .../sandbox/view`.

query.description: The text to find, matched literally. It cannot start with '-'.

paths.description: Folders to search, relative to the workspace root; the whole app when absent.

maxResults.description: The most matching lines to return; 30 by default.

actions.summary: Read a file in the app's sandbox, or list a folder.
actions.description: Reads one file of the app's code, or lists a folder's files and subfolders, so an agent sees what is there before it edits. A folder path always lists. The kernel's own files are readable; the writable boundary applies only to `POST .../sandbox/edit`.

path.description: The file or folder, relative to the workspace root.

list.description: List the path even when it is a file's folder; a folder path lists either way.

actions.summary: Check whether an app can be published now, and which build would go live.
actions.description:
Computed by the same resolver as promote-to-production. Without
`sourceRunId`: publishable iff some ready run of this project (caller's
location, main lineage) has a sealed build; the newest one goes live
with the newest config-only revision made on its lineage. With
`sourceRunId` (the reviewed preview): publishes what that preview shows —
its own sealed build, or for a ready run that built nothing, the sealed
build it descends from with config-only edits on that lineage; a run
that failed or has not finished is reviewed_preview_not_publishable. Send the returned
`sourceRunId` on promote-to-production. Tenant scope comes from the
session only.

prompt's full event log.

across pod restarts and is shared across pods.

the starters, then the vertical templates (ready-made vibe apps that
the Jenkins `vertical-templates-release` publishes). Each entry has a
stable `id`, a `category`, a human-readable `name` + `summary`, a
`version`, and the `stackTemplate` a project from it is created on.
A vertical template also names the CP Elements products it `uses`, and
its card picture when it has one (`previewUrl`). Pass the chosen `id`
as `templateId` and its `stackTemplate` on `createProject`.

actions.summary: Check a change of one kind and sign a plan for it, without writing anything.
actions.description:
The caller's AI writes a `change` of one `kind`; the server validates it
against that kind's schema and against what exists now (CRM, modules,
saved customization) and answers what applying it would do. Nothing is
written and no model is called. `planId` is a signed token over
`{projectId, locationId, kind, changeHash}` that expires at `expiresAt`;
it is `null` when `ok` is false. The location is the session's, never
the body's. Kinds: `records`, `modules`, `appearance`, `mobile`,
`assets`, `domain`; any other kind is 400 `unsupported_change_kind`
naming the supported ones. `assets` plans also return `upload`: PUT the
image bytes to `upload.url` with `upload.headers`, then apply (apply is
409 `customizer_image_not_uploaded` until they land, and the plan stays
open). `domain` apply returns the DNS records to add in
`result.dnsRecords`; `GET /custom-domains` reports when it is active.

change.description: The change, in the shape GET /changes/schema gives for `kind`.

actions.summary: Publish an app to its live site.
actions.description: Publishes the app to its live site: its managed address, and every custom domain attached to it (`changes` kind `domain`) once that domain is `active`. A domain that becomes active later joins the live site without another publish. Check `GET .../publishability` first and send the `sourceRunId` it returns, so the build the creator approved is the one that goes live. Returns a publish job: poll `GET .../infra/publish-jobs/{publishJobId}` until `status` is `succeeded` (`publishedUrl` is the live site) or `failed` (`error` says why). Send the same `idempotencyKey` to retry safely.

sourceRunId.description: Exact successful run backing the preview approved by the creator. When provided, publish fails closed instead of selecting a different run that became ready concurrently.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable retry key. Domain-aware clients should always provide one; when omitted, source-bound requests receive a deterministic server-generated key while source-less legacy requests remain independent publish attempts.

actions.summary: Publish a saved revision of an app to its members.
actions.description: For a phone app send `platform: mobile` and the `revision` from `GET .../app-config`: installed apps get it over the air. Screens your agent wrote reach members only in a new APK (`POST .../app-config/apk-builds`). `web`, the default, is for ClientPortal configuration apps; a coded web app publishes with `POST .../infra/promote-to-production`.

revision.description: The revision to publish: the app configuration's `revision`, once `appliedRevision` matches it and `status` is `ready`.

platform.description: `mobile` for a phone app. `web` (the default) publishes a ClientPortal configuration app's web revision.

actions.summary: Build a signed Android APK of a published phone app revision.
actions.description: Idempotent per Idempotency-Key. For a project whose current revision carries generated screens, the build is instead identified by the revision and the generated sources it carries (sha256(locationId:projectId:revision:sourcesSha)): repeating the request for the same revision and sources returns the same build whatever the key, and a failed one is queued again. Such a build is made from the React Native kernel commit the screens were generated against, and must be requested for the current revision. Generated screens reach members only through a new APK; they are never delivered over the air. At most one build may be active per project; sibling projects in the same location may build in parallel. Deleting a project while its build is still queued or building fails that build. A project compiles one signed APK for now: after a successful build the binary is final. A project without generated screens keeps reaching installed apps by publishing a revision; a project with generated screens cannot build another APK yet. Failed builds do not consume the allowance.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose for this build. Retrying with the same key returns the same build.

revision.description: The published revision to build. An app with generated screens builds its current revision.

actions.summary: Return a phone app to an earlier revision.
actions.description: Saves a copy of the earlier revision, screens included, as the newest one. Members get it once you publish it with `POST .../app-config/publish`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

baseRevision.description: The newest revision the caller saw (`revision` in the app's configuration). A save made since then refuses the restore instead of being overwritten.

actions.summary: Submit a prompt; the agent runs in the background.
actions.description:
Returns `runId` immediately. A sub-account token builds with its own agent: it writes the code
with `POST .../sandbox/edit` (and registers a React Native app's screens with
`POST .../sandbox/extension-routes`), saves the files with `POST .../sandbox/checkpoint`, then
starts the run with `externalAgent: true`, which checks, builds and deploys them. Poll
`GET .../runs/{runId}`: problems a passing build still has are in `checkProblems`.

The builder's own agent executes asynchronously:
attempt workspace restore from project's prior run → materialise
scaffold (only if no prior workspace) → loop tool calls → preflight
`pnpm build` → flush workspace to GCS → deploy via Cloud Build →
managed runtime revision replace → mark `ready` with a preview URL.

Per-project runtime services receive a stable public app hostname so the
iframe URL works without platform-session auth.

**Idempotency**: callers SHOULD send an `Idempotency-Key` header on
every retry. The server stores `(locationId, projectId, key)` →
`runId` for 24 h. Same key + same body → the original `runId` is
replayed. Same key + different body → `409 idempotency_conflict`.
Modeled after standard idempotent POST contracts; safe for browser
retries, network blips, and double-click submits.

**Attachment scope**: when `attachmentIds` are present, each id is
verified against the caller's tenant + project. Cross-project or
cross-tenant reuse is rejected with `403 attachment_not_owned`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Caller-generated key (UUID-v4 recommended) that makes this POST
safe to retry. Must match the prior request body byte-for-byte
on replay. Reused with a different body → `409`.

parameters.name: X-Correlation-Id
parameters.description:
Optional caller-supplied trace id. When omitted, the API mints
`cid_<uuid>` and echoes it back via the response
`X-Correlation-Id` header. Threaded through audit rows + logs.

displayText.description:
What the creator's chat bubble shows for this run instead of
`prompt`, when the client sends an instruction the creator did not
type (for example a suggestion chip, whose full text carries
verifier output or a planner directive for the agent). One plain

customCode.description:
ClientPortal-only per-run switch. When false or omitted, the agent
can inspect the project and apply SDUI configuration, but source-code,
shell, dependency, and build tools are unavailable. When true, the
existing full custom-code tool surface is enabled. This choice does
not change sandbox provisioning or preview lifecycle behavior.

clientPortalSurface.description:

Unqualified follow-ups default to this lane; explicit web, mobile,
or web-and-mobile wording in the prompt takes precedence.

externalAgent.description:
An agent outside the builder (an MCP client) writes this run's code in
the project's sandbox. The run skips the builder's agent: a first build
asks the builder's intake questions (answered through the answers
API), then every run checks, delivers, registers the sandbox with
ClientPortal, and seals a publishable release.

mobilePipelineSpeed.description:

modelId.description:
Model id from `GET /api/v1/catalog/models`. When provided, this
single model is used for every phase of the agent (classify,
plan, code). When omitted, the platform routes to its per-phase
defaults (Haiku → Sonnet → Opus).

agentId.description:
Optional id of a user-defined agent profile created via
`POST /api/v1/agents`. The profile's `systemInstructions` and
`skills` are appended to the platform's catalog for this run,
and its `defaultModelId` is honoured when `modelId` is not set.

mode.description:
Run mode. The composer's 3-way segmented control surfaces:

  - `auto` (default) — agent honours the classifier's
    `recommended_mode` and decides whether to plan, ask, or
    build straight through.
  - `plan`           — agent always proposes a plan first via
    `propose_plan` and pauses for approval. The plan is
    surfaced as a `plan_approval_request` narrator event;
    the user POSTs an approve/refine/reject verdict to
    `/agent-runs/{runId}/plan-approval`.
  - `build`          — agent skips planning and goes straight
    to file_editor (only `ask_user` when the classifier
    flags a high-cost architectural unknown).
  - `plan_first`     — back-compat alias for `plan`. v1
    callers still emit it; the runtime treats it as `plan`.

attachmentIds.description:
Optional ids of attachments previously created via
`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/attachments/upload-url`.
Surfaced to the agent as user-provided context so generated
code can reference uploaded files (logos, PDFs, brand assets).

selectedElements.description:
Visual edits (vibe apps): the elements the creator selected in the
live preview before sending. The agent receives them as a
`<selected-elements>` block after the prompt, so "this" means the
element on screen. Context only: file and line are hints the agent
checks against the workspace.

additionalPhones.description:
Add additional phone numbers to a contact. > ⚠️ **Important:** When sending `additionalPhones`, you must also include the contact’s current primary `phone` in the same request.
If you send `additionalPhones` without `phone`, the contact’s existing primary phone may be cleared or replaced.
  • phone represents the contact’s primary phone number.
  • additionalPhones represents secondary phone numbers for the same contact.
  • Always send the primary phone together with additionalPhones when updating phone numbers.
  • A maximum of 10 additional phone numbers can be provided.
  • phoneLabel is optional. Allowed values: Home, Work, Mobile, or Landline. A label can belong to only one phone number on the contact, including the primary. If a label is repeated, it is kept on the first phone number and removed from the others.
Example ```json { "phone": "+14155550100", "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Avoid ```json { "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Sending only `additionalPhones` may cause the existing primary phone number to be lost. If phone uniqueness is enabled for the location, every phone number in the request—primary and additional—must be unique across contacts. If any phone number already belongs to another contact, the request fails with **400 Bad Request** and no changes are saved.

The Upsert API will adhere to the configuration defined under the "Allow Duplicate Contact" setting at the Location level. If the setting is configured to check both Email and Phone, the API will attempt to identify an existing contact based on the priority sequence specified in the setting, and will create or update the contact accordingly.

actions.description:
Update delivery events, per-recipient statuses, and the overall message status for an email sent via a custom conversation provider.

### Authorization
- Requires the `conversations/message.write` OAuth scope.
- The calling OAuth app must own the conversation provider that originally sent the email.
- Attempts to update emails sent via LC Email or Mailgun will return `403 Forbidden`.

### Updatable Fields
All request body fields are optional. Pass only what you need to update.

**`events`** — Aggregate delivery event counters (integers). Counters are merged into the existing values (not replaced). Setting a counter to `0` is treated as no-op and will **not** reset the stored value.

**`recipients`** — Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a `MessageStatus` value. Use `failReason` to capture bounce or rejection details when the status is `failed`.

**`status`** — The overall message status. Accepts any `MessageStatus` enum value.

### Event Inference
The API automatically infers related events to maintain data consistency:
- **`clicked`, `complained`, `unsubscribed`, or `replied`** → implies `opened` (set to 1 if not already provided and open tracking is enabled) and `delivered` (set to 1).
- **`opened`** → implies `delivered` (set to 1 if not provided).
- **`delivered`, `permanent_fail`, or `temporary_fail`** → implies `accepted` (set to 1 if not provided).

### Timestamps
The API automatically records server-side timestamps on first occurrence for `delivered`, `opened`, and `clicked` events. Subsequent updates to these counters do not overwrite the original timestamp.

events.description: Aggregate delivery event counters. Counters are merged into existing values. The API automatically infers related events (e.g., reporting `clicked` will also set `opened` and `delivered` if not already present). See the endpoint description for the full inference rules.

recipients.description: Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a delivery status. Entries are upserted — if a recipient already has a status, it will be overwritten with the new value.

status.description: The overall status of the email message. Required on every request. For emails with multiple recipients, consider using the `recipients` array for granular tracking and this field for the aggregate status.

actions.description:
Post the necessary fields for the API to upload files. The files need to be a buffer with the key "fileAttachment".

Note: One of conversationId or contactId must be provided.

File Size Limits:
  • Maximum file size: 5 MB
  • Maximum files per upload: 5

Allowed file types:

Images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, HEIC, AI

Videos: MP4, MPEG, 3GP

Audio: MP3, WAV, WAVE, AIFF, AIF, AIFC, GSM, ULAW, OGG, AAC, M4A, AMR

Documents: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT

Archives: ZIP, RAR

Other: VCF, VCARD (contact files), ICS (calendar files)

The API will return an object with the URLs

Secure attachments: Set isSecureAttachment to true to upload the file as a secure attachment. This is currently supported for the email channel only; support for the remaining conversation channels is coming.

A secure attachment is returned with a /files/d/{slug} URL that is publicly accessible for one hour after upload. After that window the attachment becomes private — to render, download, or retry access, extract the {slug} from the returned URL and call GET /files/d/{slug} with a bearer token carrying the files.readonly OAuth scope, which returns a short-lived signed download URL. A file uploaded without this flag keeps its existing permanently accessible URL.

Note: From 30 November 2026 every file uploaded through this endpoint is stored as a secure attachment, and the isSecureAttachment field is ignored.

isSecureAttachment.description: Set to true to upload the file as a secure attachment. Defaults to false. Currently supported for the email channel only; support for the remaining conversation channels is coming. A secure attachment URL is publicly accessible for one hour after upload, after which the file must be fetched with GET /files/d/{slug} using the files.readonly OAuth scope. Considered only until 30 November 2026; from that date every upload is stored as a secure attachment and this field is ignored.

RETURNS: whether the delete succeeded.

Deletes one uploaded file from the authenticated location so the AI no longer uses it.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to remove a document; use getFilesByKnowledgeBasePublic to find the file id; use deleteTrainedUrlsForKnowledgeBase for crawled pages instead.
RETURNS: whether the delete succeeded.

Permanently deletes a knowledge base and its associated trained content.

actions.description:
Removes trained website pages from a knowledge base so the AI no longer references them.

RETURNS: whether the delete succeeded.

excludeUrlIds.description: URL IDs to exclude from a deleteAll operation (select-all-minus-some flow)

Requires `limit`; pass body `searchAfter` from the previous response `searchAfter` (opaque base64url string) for the next page. Scope to lists with `listIds` (max 10) — do not send a separate `graph` filter when using `listIds`. Filter subtasks with `parentTaskId` (Tasks V2 locations only; otherwise 422). `subtaskViewMode=expanded` returns embedded `subtasks[]`; `separate` may include `parentName`. Neither field appears on Get/Create/Update/List/Batch. `total` is the hit count after filters and access scope.

query.description: Free-text search across searchable task properties (max 75 characters)

filters.description: Prefer `listIds` to scope a query to lists. Otherwise each item is a Filter (`field`, `operator`, `value`) or a GroupFilter (`group`: `AND` | `OR`, nested `filters`). Operators: `eq`, `not_eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `contains_set`, `range`, `nested`, `exists`, `not_exists`. Task fields: `status`, `assignees`, `parentTaskId`, `dueDate`, `startDate`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `contactId`, `businessId`, plus custom-field keys. Unknown field or operator is rejected by search (422). Groups may nest. Do not combine `listIds` with a `graph` filter.

listIds.description: List ids to scope the search (max 10). Equivalent to one nested `graph` filter (`type=list`, `id` eq or `contains_set`). More than 10 ids, a non-list target, or a second graph scope returns **422** (`error`: `graph_scope_invalid`).

subtaskViewMode.description: How subtasks appear. Allowed: `collapsed` (parents only), `expanded` (parents with embedded `subtasks[]`), `separate` (subtasks as their own records with `parentTaskId` / `parentName`). Requires a Tasks V2 / Kanban location. On any other location this field, or a `parentTaskId` filter, returns **422**. `parentName` and `subtasks` are search-only — Get Task By ID, Get Tasks, and Fetch Tasks By IDs do not populate them. `total` is the hit count after filters and access scope (post-RBAC). Page with `searchAfter` until it is null.

actions.description:
Apply a watermark to an image using either a specific template ID or by resolving the template bound to a specific connected account.

If the same watermark + image combination has been processed before, the response returns immediately with `status: completed` and the output URL in `message`. Otherwise, processing is queued and the response returns `status: pending` with a `progressId`.

**Rate limits:** This endpoint may be rate-limited to prevent abuse. To resolve a template dynamically at publish time, pass `accountId` — the endpoint will resolve the template bound to that connected account. Use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint to look up account IDs.

Processing is asynchronous — the response returns a `progressId` that identifies this preview job.

**Document fields:**
- `status`: 'pending' | 'processing' | 'completed' | 'failed'
- `outputMediaUrl`: string, available when `status` is `completed`
- `errorMessage`: string, available when `status` is `failed`

templateId.description: Template ID to apply. Required if `accountId` is not provided.

accountId.description: Connected account ID — the endpoint will resolve the template bound to this account. Required if `templateId` is not provided. Use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint to look up account IDs.

inputMediaUrl.description: Input media URL (either video or image)

postId.description: Optional post ID to associate the watermark output with

watermarkId.description: Optional cache key to fetch a previously-generated watermark result

actions.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 3: Connect the Account

This is the final step in the OAuth flow. After retrieving available accounts (Step 2), use this endpoint to connect the selected account to your location.

### OAuth Flow Summary

1. **Start OAuth** → User authenticates with platform
2. **Get Accounts** → Retrieved available pages/channels
3. **Attach Account** (this endpoint) → Connect the selected account

### Request Body

The accepted fields depend on the `platform` path parameter — pick the matching schema in the request body below. Most platforms take the `originId`, `name` and optional `avatar` of the account you selected in Step 2; Google Business Profile takes the full `location` and `account` objects.

> `tiktok-business` accounts are connected through the TikTok Business flow, not this endpoint.

### After Connection

Once connected, the account will appear in your location's connected accounts and can be used for social media posting.

parameters.description: Social media platform. Must match the platform used in the preceding steps of the OAuth flow.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: The Location ID where you want to connect this social account

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The OAuth Account ID received from Step 1 (Start OAuth) via the window message event

type.description: Type of Facebook account (must be page)

name.description: Name of the Facebook page or account

actions.description:
Create a top-level comment on a post (`isParentThread: true`, `parentId` = postId) or a reply to an existing comment (`isParentThread: false`, `parentId` = commentId). Per-platform content max length: Facebook 8000, Instagram 2200, Linkedin 3000, Community 8000, Tiktok 150, Bluesky 300, Youtube 10000, Threads 500.

**Optional-field platform support:**
- `attachments` — supported on **Facebook only**. Ignored on Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Bluesky, Community (Community processes the field but external URLs are not rendered due to its bucket restriction).
- `mentions` — supported on **Facebook**, **LinkedIn**, and **Community** only. Ignored on Instagram, TikTok, Bluesky.
- `notifyAllGroupMembers` — supported on **Community** only. When `true`, all group members get a push/in-app notification (equivalent to an `@everyone` broadcast). Independent of the `mentions` array and of `@everyone` text in `content`. Default `false`.

parentId.description: For top-level comments (`isParentThread: true`): pass the post ID returned by the posts API. For replies (`isParentThread: false`): pass the parent comment ID returned by the list-comments API. In both cases this must be a valid 24-character internal ID — not the native platform ID.

isParentThread.description: Set `true` to create a top-level comment on a post (parentId = post ID). Set `false` to create a reply to an existing comment (parentId = comment ID).

content.description: Content of the comment. Per-platform max length: Facebook 8000, Instagram 2200, Linkedin 3000, Community 8000, Tiktok 150, Bluesky 300, Youtube 10000, Threads 500.

attachments.description: Attachments for the comment (max 1 image). **Supported on:** Facebook only. **Not supported on:** Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Bluesky, Community — the field is accepted by the API but the attachment will not appear on the comment. (Community processes the field server-side, but external URLs are not rendered due to its bucket restriction.)

mentions.description:
Mentions for the comment. **Supported on:** Facebook, LinkedIn, Community. **Ignored on:** Instagram, TikTok, Bluesky — the field is accepted but mentions are not rendered on these platforms.

`offset`/`length` must locate `name` inside `content` exactly — `content.substring(offset, offset + length) === name` — otherwise the request is rejected with 400. The example below aligns with the `content` example above.

notifyAllGroupMembers.description:
When `true`, all members of the Community group receive a push/in-app notification about this comment — equivalent to an `@everyone` broadcast.

**Supported on:** Community only. Ignored on all other platforms (the field is accepted but no notification is sent).

**Independent of the `mentions` array** — you do not need to add an `@everyone` entry to `mentions` for this to take effect. Conversely, putting the literal text `@everyone` in `content` does **not** by itself trigger notifications; only this flag does.

Defaults to `false` (no broadcast notification). Use `true` only when the comment is genuinely intended for every member of the group — overuse may cause members to mute the group.

pollOptions.description: Poll options for Threads reply (2-4 options)

textAttachment.description: Text attachment for Threads reply with optional styling info

threadLocationId.description: Location ID for Threads reply location tagging

actions.description:
Create posts for all supported platforms. It is possible to create customized posts per channel by using the same platform account IDs in a request and hitting the create post API multiple times with different summaries and account IDs per platform.

The content and media limitations, as well as platform rate limiters corresponding to the respective platforms, are provided in the following reference link:

  Link: [Platform Limitations](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations "Social Planner Help")

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Location ID (also known as Sub-Account ID) for the business location.

accountIds.description:
Account IDs for the post. Each account ID identifies a connected social media account.

**Get IDs from:** [Get Accounts API](/social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/accounts) — use the `id` field from each account.

**One request = one post, shared across every account in this list.**
- All accounts share the same `summary` and the same `media` array.
- `summary` is trimmed to the **strictest** character limit among the selected platforms. Adding a Bluesky account (300 chars) therefore trims the caption to 300 for Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn in that same request.
- `media` is capped to each platform's own maximum at publish time (e.g. Bluesky publishes the first 4 items, Instagram the first 10).
- **To keep full-length, platform-specific captions, send one request per platform** - one post per platform, each with only that platform's account IDs.

**Validations:**
- Required for non-draft posts
- Must be a non-empty array
- All account IDs must be valid connected accounts for the location

summary.description:
Post content/caption text. Character limits vary by platform.

**Custom Values & Hashtags:**
- You can include custom values/variables in the content (e.g., `{{contact.name}}`)
- Hashtags: Use `#hashtag` format. Instagram allows max 30 hashtags.
- Mentions: Use platform-specific mention format (see `mentions` field for structured mentions)

**Validations:**
- Instagram/Facebook Story: Caption NOT supported for direct publishing
- Facebook, LinkedIn, GMB: Content OR media is required (at least one)

**Trimming across multiple platforms:**
One post carries ONE caption for every account in `accountIds`, so the caption is silently trimmed to the **strictest** limit among the selected platforms — not to each platform's own limit.
- Facebook 63,206 · LinkedIn 3,000 · Instagram / TikTok 2,200 · Google 1,500 · Pinterest 800 · Threads 500 · **Bluesky 300**
- Example: `accountIds` covering Facebook + Instagram + Bluesky trims the caption to **300 characters on all three**.
- Instagram/Facebook Stories without push-notification publishing force the limit to 0, dropping the caption entirely.
- **To keep the full caption on each platform, send one request per platform** instead of one request mixing platforms.

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)
summary.example: Hello World! Check out our latest updates. #social #marketing

media.description:
Post Media Data. Per-platform media limits are listed in the reference link in the API description.

**Across multiple platforms:** the same media array is sent to every account in `accountIds` and capped to each platform's own maximum at publish time — the array is NOT reduced to the strictest limit the way `summary` is. An 8-item array publishes 8 items to Facebook and the first 4 to Bluesky.
Send one request per platform if a platform needs a different set of media.

status.description:
Post status indicating the current state of the post.

**Available Status Values:**
- `draft` - Post saved as draft, not yet ready for publishing
- `scheduled` - Post scheduled for future publishing (requires `scheduleDate`)
- `in_review` - Post pending approval (requires `scheduleDate` and `postApprovalDetails`)
- `published` - Post has been published
- `in_progress` - Post is currently being processed
- `pending` - Post is awaiting platform processing for Instagram media container creation
- `failed` - Post publishing failed
- `notification_sent` - Story notification sent (for manual story posting)
- `deleted` - Post has been deleted

**Validations:**
- `scheduled` or `in_review` status requires `scheduleDate` to be set
- Submitting for review (`in_review`) requires `postApprovalDetails.approver`; approve/reject actions reuse the stored approver
- Draft posts skip most validations (accountIds, media requirements)

scheduleDate.description: Schedule Date. Required when `status` is `scheduled` or `in_review`.

selectedBestTime.description: Selected Best Time slot for scheduling

createdBy.description:
User ID of the creator who is creating/managing the post. Must be a valid 24-character hex ID.

**Get User IDs from:** [Get User API](/users/{userId}) — use the `id` field from the user object.

**Validation:** Must be a valid 24-character hex ID.

followUpComment.description:
Follow-up comment to be posted immediately after the main post is published.

**Supported Platforms:** Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Community, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube, TikTok

**NOT Supported:** GBP (Google Business Profile), Pinterest

- TikTok: posted once the video becomes publicly viewable (~1-3 min), not instantly

- TikTok: only public videos support a follow-up comment. Set `privacyLevel` to `PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE` — friends-only and private videos are not supported

**Use Case:** Great for adding hashtags, additional context, or engagement prompts without cluttering the main post.

- Like `summary`, the follow-up comment is trimmed to the **strictest** limit among the post's platforms, not to each platform's own limit — a post that includes Bluesky (300) trims the comment to 300 everywhere. Send one request per platform to keep the full comment on each.

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

type.description:
Type of post to create. Determines the format and platform requirements.

**Available Types:**
- `post` - Standard feed post (all platforms)
- `story` - Temporary 24-hour story (Instagram, Facebook)
- `reel` - Short-form video content (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube)

**Customize Per Platform:**
You can specify different content/types per platform using `facebookPostDetails.type`, `instagramPostDetails.type`, etc.

**Validations:**
- Reels require exactly 1 video
- Stories: Caption not supported for Instagram/Facebook
- Facebook Groups do not support Reels

scheduleTimeUpdated.description: Flag indicating if the schedule datetime was manually updated. Used for tracking rescheduled posts.

tags.description:
Array of Tag IDs to associate with the post for organization and filtering.

**Get Tag IDs from:** [Get Tags API](/social-media-posting/{locationId}/tags) — use the `_id` field from each tag.

**Validation:** All IDs must be valid 24-character hex IDs.

categoryId.description:
Category ID to organize the post. Categories help group related posts.

**Get Category IDs from:** [Get Categories API](/social-media-posting/{locationId}/categories) — use the `_id` field.

**Validation:** Must be a valid 24-character hex ID.

applyWatermark.description:
Apply watermark to media in this post.

**Note:** Watermarks are applied to images only. Videos are not watermarked.

userId.description: User ID of the user creating/managing the post. Required for OAuth channel posts (non-draft).

linkedinPostDetails.description:
LinkedIn-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `postAsPdf`: Set to `true` to post images as a PDF carousel document
- `pdfTitle`: Title for the PDF document (max 100 characters)

**Limits:**
- Max 9 images/videos for regular posts
- Max 300 pages for PDF carousel
- Max PDF size: 100 MB

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

pinterestPostDetails.description:
Pinterest-specific post configuration. Required when posting to Pinterest accounts.

**Required Fields:**
- `boardIds`: Object mapping account OAuth IDs to Pinterest board IDs

**Optional Fields:**
- `title`: Pin title (max 100 characters)
- `link`: Destination URL for the pin (max 2048 characters)

**Get Board IDs:** Use the Pinterest boards API or retrieve from connected account details.

**Limits:**
- Max 1 image/video per pin
- Caption max 800 characters

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

facebookPostDetails.description:
Facebook-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `type`: Post type (`post`, `story`, `reel`)

**Restrictions:**
- Facebook Groups do NOT support Reels
- Reels require exactly 1 video
- Stories do not support captions

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

instagramPostDetails.description:
Instagram-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `type`: Post type (`post`, `story`, `reel`)
- `collaborators`: Map of account IDs to Instagram usernames for collaboration invites (max 5 per account)
- `showOnFeed`: Show reel on profile feed (for reels)

**Collaborators Structure:**
```json
{ "accountId": ["username1", "username2"] }
```
Where `accountId` is from [Get Accounts API](/social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/accounts) and usernames are Instagram handles without @.

**Restrictions:**
- Media is REQUIRED for all Instagram posts
- Max 30 hashtags allowed in caption
- Stories do not support captions
- Collaborators: Posts/Reels only (NOT Stories)
- Reels require exactly 1 video

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

youtubePostDetails.description:
YouTube-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `title`: Video title (max 100 characters)
- `type`: Video type (`video` for regular videos, `short` for YouTube Shorts)
- `privacyLevel`: Video visibility (`private`, `public`, `unlisted`)

**Limits:**
- Max 1 video per post
- Caption (description) max 5,000 characters

**Requirements:**
- Video is REQUIRED for YouTube posts
- `type` field is required

communityPostDetails.description:
Community-specific post configuration for Communities.

**Required Fields:**
- `title`: Post title (max 1,000 characters)
- `postAsUser`: the member to publish as, keyed by Community account ID

**Optional Fields:**
- `notifyAllGroupMembers`: notify all group members (`@everyone` broadcast)

**Limits:**
- Max 4 media items
- Caption max 100,000 characters

**Required when** `accountIds` contains a Community account and the post is not a draft.

timeSlots.description: Time slots defining when posts should be published

enableFuturePosts.description: Enable Future Posts. Defaults to false.

prioritizeNewContent.description: Prioritize New Content. Defaults to false.

userId.description: User id

actions.summary: Create a new item in the queue
actions.description: Adds a new post item to a queue. Use sessionId for edit session or directToQueue for immediate addition.

order.description:
Order for the new item in the queue (cyclic-aware). Accepts:
- A number: explicit order value calculated by FE as midpoint between adjacent items
- "top": place at cyclic top (first to be scheduled next)
- "bottom": place at cyclic bottom (last to be scheduled)

For positions between items, FE calculates: Math.floor((prevItem.order + nextItem.order) / 2)
Defaults to end if not provided. Note: This field is ignored when directToQueue is true -
the order will be automatically calculated based on the queue's prioritizeNewContent setting.

primaryImage.description: Primary media URL (image) for the post. Falls back to modifiedPostPayload.primaryImage if not set.

directToQueue.description: When true, creates the queue item directly without requiring an edit session, even for active/paused queues. The order field is ignored and the item position is determined by the queue's prioritizeNewContent setting: if true, the item is added to the top of the queue; if false, it is added to the bottom.

actions.description:
Create a new reusable watermark template for a location. The template stores the watermark image URL, position, scale, opacity, padding, and the connected accounts it applies to.

At post-publish time, the template is resolved for a given connected account via the `accountIds` binding — the `accountId` you provide here maps a connected social account to this template. To fetch account IDs, use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint.

watermarkImageUrl.description: URL of the watermark image. Must be a PNG or JPG file, minimum 200x200 pixels, and no larger than 5 MB.

position.description: Watermark position. Position can be one of the following values: top-left, top-center, top-right, left-center, center, right-center, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right

scale.description: Scale factor for watermark. scale value must be between 0 - 1

opacity.description: Watermark opacity. opacity value must be between 0 - 1

padding.description: Whether padding is applied around the watermark

accountIds.description: Connected account IDs to bind this template to. These IDs map user accounts to this template at post-publish time. Use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint to look up account IDs.

facebookPostDetails.description:
Facebook-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `type`: Post type (`post`, `story`, `reel`)

**Restrictions:**
- Facebook Groups do NOT support Reels
- Reels require exactly 1 video
- Stories do not support captions

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

instagramPostDetails.description:
Instagram-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `type`: Post type (`post`, `story`, `reel`)
- `collaborators`: Map of account IDs to Instagram usernames for collaboration invites (max 5 per account)
- `showOnFeed`: Show reel on profile feed (for reels)

**Collaborators Structure:**
```json
{ "accountId": ["username1", "username2"] }
```
Where `accountId` is from [Get Accounts API](/social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/accounts) and usernames are Instagram handles without @.

**Restrictions:**
- Media is REQUIRED for all Instagram posts
- Max 30 hashtags allowed in caption
- Stories do not support captions
- Collaborators: Posts/Reels only (NOT Stories)
- Reels require exactly 1 video

**Reference:** [Platform Limitations Guide](https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/48001240003-social-planner-image-video-content-and-api-limitations)

youtubePostDetails.description:
YouTube-specific post configuration.

**Key Fields:**
- `title`: Video title (max 100 characters)
- `type`: Video type (`video` for regular videos, `short` for YouTube Shorts)
- `privacyLevel`: Video visibility (`private`, `public`, `unlisted`)

**Limits:**
- Max 1 video per post
- Caption (description) max 5,000 characters

**Requirements:**
- Video is REQUIRED for YouTube posts
- `type` field is required

communityPostDetails.description:
Community-specific post configuration for Communities.

**Required Fields:**
- `title`: Post title (max 1,000 characters)
- `postAsUser`: the member to publish as, keyed by Community account ID

**Optional Fields:**

**Limits:**

- Caption max 100,000 characters

**Required when** `accountIds` contains a Community account and the post is not a draft.

actions.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 2: Get Available Accounts

After completing OAuth authentication (Step 1), use this endpoint to retrieve the list of available pages, channels, or locations that can be connected.

### OAuth Flow Position

1. **Start OAuth** → User authenticates, returns `accountId`
2. **Get Accounts** (this endpoint) → Lists available pages/channels to connect
3. **Attach Account** → Connect the selected account

### What This Returns

The response varies by platform:

| Platform | Returns |
|----------|--------|
| **facebook** | List of Facebook Pages the user manages |
| **instagram** | List of Instagram Professional Accounts (linked to Facebook Pages) |
| **google** | Google Business Profile locations |
| **linkedin** | LinkedIn Pages and Profile |
| **tiktok** | TikTok Creator account info |
| **tiktok-business** | TikTok Business Center accounts |
| **youtube** | YouTube Channels |
| **pinterest** | Pinterest Business accounts and boards |
| **threads** | Threads profiles |

### Next Step

From the response, select the account/page you want to connect and use its details in Step 3:
```
POST /social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
```

## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 1: Initiate OAuth

This is the first step in the 3-step OAuth flow to connect a social media account:

1. **Start OAuth** (this endpoint) → User authenticates with the platform
2. **Get Accounts** → Retrieve available pages/channels to connect
3. **Attach Account** → Connect the selected account to your location

### How to Use

Open this API in a browser window (not via cURL) with the required query parameters. The user will be redirected to the platform's OAuth login screen.

### Receiving the OAuth Response

After successful authentication, the OAuth window will post a message back to your application. Listen for this message to get the `accountId` needed for the next step.

```javascript
window.addEventListener('message', function(e) {
  if (e.data && e.data.page === 'social_media_posting') {
    const { actionType, page, platform, placement, accountId, reconnectAccounts } = e.data;
    // Use accountId for Step 2: GET /oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
  }
}, false);
```

### Event Data Response

| Field | Type | Example | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| actionType | string | "close" | The action type |
| page | string | "social-media-posting" | Source page identifier |
| platform | string | "facebook" | The OAuth platform |
| placement | string | "placement" | Placement context |
| accountId | string | "658a9b6833b91e0ecb8f3958" | **Use this for Step 2** |
| reconnectAccounts | string[] | ["658a9b...", "efd2da..."] | Accounts that need reconnection |

### Next Step

Use the `accountId` from the response to call:
```
GET /social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
```

### Platform Notes

- **bluesky**: Currently not supported, will return an error
- **tiktok-business**: Uses a separate business OAuth flow

actions.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Count the log records of one workflow, grouped by one or more dimensions. It answers how many: enrollments, completions, failures per step, why contacts left, and trends over time. To answer who, use Get Workflow Logs.

**Before you call it.** Get `workflowId` from Search Workflows. Never pass a workflow name.

**Grouping.** Each row holds one value for every dimension in `groupBy`, plus `count`. Grouping by `week`, `day` or `hour` adds `bucket`, the start of each interval in `timezone`. `startDate` and `endDate` always stay UTC. Rows are sorted by the grouped values in ascending order (`status`, then `type`, `stepId`, `removedReason` and `bucket`), not by count.

**Finding filter values.** Group by a dimension to see which values this workflow has, then filter on them. For example, `groupBy=removedReason` lists the reasons present, and those values work in `removedReasons`.

**Steps.** Rows grouped by `stepId` also carry `stepName`, the name of that step on its most recent log record in the date range. `stepId` matches `actions[].id` in Get Workflow Definition. A step count includes the `remove_from_workflow` record written when a contact leaves the workflow at that step, so group by `stepId` and `type` together to count how often the step itself ran.

**Common questions.**
- Enrollments: `statuses=added_to_workflow`
- Completions: `removedReasons=end_of_workflow`. Divide by enrollments for a completion rate
- Failures per step: `statuses=error,failed,failed_retry_limit_reached&groupBy=stepId`
- Why contacts left: `types=remove_from_workflow&groupBy=removedReason`
- Stopped because the contact replied: `removedReasons=contact_reply_stop_response`
- Goal reached: `types=workflow_goal&statuses=success`
- Enrollment trend: `statuses=added_to_workflow&groupBy=week` (or `day`)
- Change over time: call twice with back-to-back windows of equal length and compare

Completions in a window can include contacts who enrolled before it, so a completion rate can exceed 100%. With fewer than about 30 enrollments, rates swing widely. Zero is a real answer. A `workflowId` that does not exist in the sub-account returns 404.

**Limits.** The range defaults to the last 30 days and must not exceed 30 days. Logs are available for the last 60 days. A grouping that produces more rows than `limit` is refused with 422 rather than truncated, because a truncated count reports wrong totals.

**Compatibility.** New optional fields and new values of `status`, `type` and `removedReason` can appear at any time. Ignore fields you do not know, and treat an unknown value as other.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Workflow ID. Get it from Search Workflows. Never pass a workflow name

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Sub-account (location) ID. It must be the sub-account the token belongs to, otherwise the request is refused with 403

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the range, ISO 8601: a plain date (start of that day, UTC) or a full timestamp. Send it together with endDate. Defaults to 30 days ago. Logs are available for the last 60 days, so it cannot be earlier than that

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the range, ISO 8601. A plain date includes the whole day. At most 30 days after startDate. Defaults to now

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: Dimensions to group the counts by. Repeat the parameter or send a comma-separated list. `status` is the step outcome, `type` the step type, `stepId` the step, `removedReason` why the contact left the workflow, and `week`, `day` or `hour` a time bucket (one at most). Defaults to `status`

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Count only these step outcomes. Values: `added_to_workflow` (the contact entered the workflow), `success` (the step ran), `error` and `failed` (the step did not complete), `failed_retry_limit_reached` (the step gave up after its retries), `retry` (the step will run again), `skipped` (the step did not run, for example because of DND, a time window or missing data), `waiting` (the contact is waiting at the step), `wait_finished` (a wait ended), `finished` (the contact left the workflow, see removedReason), `paused_due_to_draft_mode` (the workflow was unpublished while the contact was in it), `contact_merged` (the contact was merged into another contact), `drip_queued` (the contact is waiting in a drip step for its batch), `drip_resume` (the batch was released and the contact moved on), `processing` (the step has started and has not finished yet), and `winner_declared` (an A/B test step picked its winning path; the record has no contact). New values can appear. Group by `status` first to see the values this workflow has

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Count only these step types: a step `type` key, as listed by Get Step Types or in `actions[].type` of Get Workflow Definition. Unlike Get Workflow Logs, `if_else` and `drip` match only those exact keys here. New values can appear. Group by `type` first to see the types this workflow has

parameters.name: removedReasons
parameters.description: Count only records removed for these reasons. Values: `end_of_workflow` (the contact reached the end), `contact_deleted` (the contact was deleted), `deleted_workflow` (the workflow was deleted), `record_deleted` (the record was deleted), `goal_action` (a goal step removed the contact), `contact_reply_stop_response` (the contact replied and the workflow stops on reply), `contact_merge` (the contact was merged), `appointment-change`, `invoice-change` and `service-booking-change` (the appointment, invoice or booking changed and the workflow restarted for the contact), `attendee-change` (the Events attendee or their event changed, and the run for that attendee ended), `rental-booking-change` (the rental booking that started the workflow was deleted or cancelled), `wait_step_window_in_past` (a wait step time window pointed to a time in the past, so the contact left), and `missing-data` (the step the contact was on was deleted from the workflow). Values are exact, including the ones with hyphens. New values can appear. Group by `removedReason` first to see the values this workflow has

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA timezone for the week, day and hour buckets. It does not move startDate and endDate, which stay UTC. Defaults to UTC

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of grouped rows. A grouping that produces more is refused with 422 rather than truncated. Default 1000, maximum 5000

actions.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

List the step-by-step execution history of one workflow, newest first. Each record is one step of one run for one contact or record, with its outcome and timing. It answers who and what: who entered, what happened to a contact, which steps failed and for whom. To answer how many, use Get Workflow Log Statistics.

**Before you call it.** Get `workflowId` from Search Workflows. Never pass a workflow name. To see what each step is, call Get Workflow Definition: its `actions[].id` matches `stepId` here.

**Step details.** `meta` says how the contact entered, why a step was skipped or failed, what a step did, whether a wait timed out, and why the contact left. A key is left out when it does not apply. Only the keys documented under `meta` are returned. New keys may be added later (see Compatibility).

**Paging.** The response holds `logs`, their `count`, and `nextCursor`. The first call (`action=first`, the default) returns the newest page. For the next (older) page, send `action=next` with `referenceId` and `referenceCreatedAt` from `nextCursor`, unchanged, and keep the same filters and dates. `nextCursor` is null when there are no more records. A cursor that does not match returns 422. A page holds at most 100 records, 15 by default.

**Dates.** Send `startDate` and `endDate` together (ISO 8601, UTC, at most 30 days apart). Without them, the last 30 days are returned. Logs are available for the last 60 days.

**Common questions.**
- Who entered the workflow: `statuses=added_to_workflow`
- Which steps failed, and for whom: `statuses=error,failed,failed_retry_limit_reached`
- What happened to one contact: `contactId=<contact ID>`
- Every step of one run: `executionId=<workflowStatusId of any record from that run>`

An empty `logs` list is a real answer: nothing matched in that window. A `workflowId` that does not exist in the sub-account, or is a folder, returns 404.

**Compatibility.** New optional fields, including new `meta` keys, and new values of `status`, `type` and `recordType` can appear at any time. Ignore fields you do not know, and treat an unknown value as other.

For every kind of failure, send `error`, `failed` and `failed_retry_limit_reached`. New values can appear

Replace a workflow definition in full. **This is a complete overwrite** — any step absent from the request is deleted, so always read the current definition first and send it back modified — the definition carries its own `version`, so sending back what you read keeps you protected against overwriting a concurrent edit. A stale `version` is rejected with 422 and nothing is written.

**Draft only.** A published workflow is rejected with 409: the overwrite would replace steps under contacts currently moving through it. Set the workflow to draft with Update Workflow Status, update it, then publish it again.

**Order matters.** Changing status advances the `version`, so read the definition *after* setting the workflow to draft: draft → read → update → publish. Reading first and drafting second leaves you holding a stale `version`.

additionalPhones.description:
Add additional phone numbers to a contact. > ⚠️ **Important:** When sending `additionalPhones`, you must also include the contact’s current primary `phone` in the same request.
If you send `additionalPhones` without `phone`, the contact’s existing primary phone may be cleared or replaced.
  • phone represents the contact’s primary phone number.
  • additionalPhones represents secondary phone numbers for the same contact.
  • Always send the primary phone together with additionalPhones when updating phone numbers.
  • A maximum of 10 additional phone numbers can be provided.
  • phoneLabel is optional. Allowed values: Home, Work, Mobile, or Landline. A label can belong to only one phone number on the contact, including the primary. If a label is repeated, it is kept on the first phone number and removed from the others.
Example ```json { "phone": "+14155550100", "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Avoid ```json { "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Sending only `additionalPhones` may cause the existing primary phone number to be lost. If phone uniqueness is enabled for the location, every phone number in the request—primary and additional—must be unique across contacts. If any phone number already belongs to another contact, the request fails with **400 Bad Request** and no changes are saved.

The Upsert API will adhere to the configuration defined under the “Allow Duplicate Contact” setting at the Location level. If the setting is configured to check both Email and Phone, the API will attempt to identify an existing contact based on the priority sequence specified in the setting, and will create or update the contact accordingly.

If two separate contacts already exist—one with the same email and another with the same phone—and an upsert request includes both the email and phone, the API will update the contact that matches the first field in the configured sequence, and ignore the second field to prevent duplication.

Export messages for a specific location with cursor-based pagination support.

**Channel Filtering Behavior:**
- **When channel is omitted:** Returns all non-email message types, including messages that don't belong to any specific channel.
- **When channel=Email:** Returns email messages only.
- **When channel is specified (SMS, Call, WhatsApp, etc.):** Returns messages for that specific channel.

**Limitations:**
- Group Chat and SMS Review Request message types are not supported.
- Activity messages (opportunity updates, appointments, etc.) are not included in the export. Use `GET /conversations/{conversationId}/messages` (Get messages by conversation id) to fetch them.
- Cursor validity is 2 minutes from the last request made.

actions.description:
Update delivery events, per-recipient statuses, and the overall message status for an email sent via a custom conversation provider.

### Authorization
- Requires the `conversations/message.write` OAuth scope.
- The calling OAuth app must own the conversation provider that originally sent the email.
- Attempts to update emails sent via LC Email or Mailgun will return `403 Forbidden`.

### Updatable Fields
All request body fields are optional. Pass only what you need to update.

**`events`** — Aggregate delivery event counters (integers). Counters are merged into the existing values (not replaced). Setting a counter to `0` is treated as no-op and will **not** reset the stored value.

**`recipients`** — Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a `MessageStatus` value. Use `failReason` to capture bounce or rejection details when the status is `failed`.

**`status`** — The overall message status. Accepts any `MessageStatus` enum value.

### Event Inference
The API automatically infers related events to maintain data consistency:
- **`clicked`, `complained`, `unsubscribed`, or `replied`** → implies `opened` (set to 1 if not already provided and open tracking is enabled) and `delivered` (set to 1).
- **`opened`** → implies `delivered` (set to 1 if not provided).
- **`delivered`, `permanent_fail`, or `temporary_fail`** → implies `accepted` (set to 1 if not provided).

### Timestamps
The API automatically records server-side timestamps on first occurrence for `delivered`, `opened`, and `clicked` events. Subsequent updates to these counters do not overwrite the original timestamp.

events.description: Aggregate delivery event counters. Counters are merged into existing values. The API automatically infers related events (e.g., reporting `clicked` will also set `opened` and `delivered` if not already present). See the endpoint description for the full inference rules.

recipients.description: Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a delivery status. Entries are upserted — if a recipient already has a status, it will be overwritten with the new value.

status.description: The overall status of the email message. Required on every request. For emails with multiple recipients, consider using the `recipients` array for granular tracking and this field for the aggregate status.

actions.description:
Post the necessary fields for the API to upload files. The files need to be a buffer with the key "fileAttachment".

Note: One of conversationId or contactId must be provided.

File Size Limits:
  • Maximum file size: 5 MB
  • Maximum files per upload: 5

Allowed file types:

Images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, HEIC, AI

Videos: MP4, MPEG, 3GP

Audio: MP3, WAV, WAVE, AIFF, AIF, AIFC, GSM, ULAW, OGG, AAC, M4A, AMR

Documents: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT

Archives: ZIP, RAR

Other: VCF, VCARD (contact files), ICS (calendar files)

The API will return an object with the URLs

Secure attachments: Set isSecureAttachment to true to upload the file as a secure attachment. This is currently supported for the email channel only; support for the remaining conversation channels is coming.

A secure attachment is returned with a /files/d/{slug} URL that is publicly accessible for one hour after upload. After that window the attachment becomes private — to render, download, or retry access, extract the {slug} from the returned URL and call GET /files/d/{slug} with a bearer token carrying the files.readonly OAuth scope, which returns a short-lived signed download URL. A file uploaded without this flag keeps its existing permanently accessible URL.

Note: From 30 November 2026 every file uploaded through this endpoint is stored as a secure attachment, and the isSecureAttachment field is ignored.

isSecureAttachment.description: Set to true to upload the file as a secure attachment. Defaults to false. Currently supported for the email channel only; support for the remaining conversation channels is coming. A secure attachment URL is publicly accessible for one hour after upload, after which the file must be fetched with GET /files/d/{slug} using the files.readonly OAuth scope. Considered only until 30 November 2026; from that date every upload is stored as a secure attachment and this field is ignored.

actions.description: Creates a new pipeline with at least one stage for a given location. Pipeline names must be unique per location (case-insensitive), and stage names must be unique within the pipeline. To enable manual win probability, set `useOpportunityProbability` to `true` and provide a `stageWinProbability` (0–100) on every stage — if any stage is missing a value, the system falls back to auto-computed probabilities based on stage position.

position.description: 0-based display order. REQUIRED: without it GHL answers 422 "stages.N.position should not be empty" and creates nothing (measured live 2026-09-28).

stageWinProbability.description: Win probability 0-100. Give EVERY stage one: if any stage omits it, GHL discards all of them and stores an even ramp ((i + 1) / (n + 1) * 100) whatever useOpportunityProbability says (measured live 2026-09-28: 11, missing, 33 was stored as 25, 50, 75).

notes: Proven live 2026-09-28: every stage needs `position` (else 422, nothing created), and give every stage a stageWinProbability (if one is missing GHL replaces them all with an even ramp).

actions.description: Update Opportunity Status

Updates an existing pipeline. The `stages` array is a full replacement — include the `id` field on existing stages to retain them, or omit it to create a new stage. You cannot remove all stages at once. Any opportunities in removed stages are automatically migrated to the lowest-position remaining stage. Pipeline and stage names must remain unique (case-insensitive) within the location. Documentation Link - https://doc.clickup.com/8631005/d/h/87cpx-709536/75a21483123abd7

id.description: Existing stage ID. Include it to preserve the stage (and its opportunities); omit for new stages.

actions.description: Searches tasks across the location with filters, sort, free-text `query`, and optional `subtaskViewMode`. Requires `limit`; pass body `searchAfter` from the previous response `searchAfter` (opaque base64url string) for the next page. Scope to lists with `listIds` (max 10) — do not send a separate `graph` filter when using `listIds`. Filter subtasks with `parentTaskId` (Tasks V2 locations only; otherwise 422). `subtaskViewMode=expanded` returns embedded `subtasks[]`; `separate` may include `parentName`. Neither field appears on Get/Create/Update/List/Batch. `total` is the hit count after filters and access scope.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Location id. **Required for `channel: APP`.** Ignored for OAuth/PIT — those use the location on the auth token. Do not send in path, body, or headers.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks per page

searchAfter.description: Opaque searchAfter from the previous response `searchAfter` (base64url-encoded JSON array). Pass the string back verbatim. A legacy decoded JSON array is also accepted.

query.description: Free-text search across searchable task properties (max 75 characters)

filters.description: Prefer `listIds` to scope a query to lists. Otherwise each item is a Filter (`field`, `operator`, `value`) or a GroupFilter (`group`: `AND` | `OR`, nested `filters`). Operators: `eq`, `not_eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `contains_set`, `range`, `nested`, `exists`, `not_exists`. Task fields: `status`, `assignees`, `parentTaskId`, `dueDate`, `startDate`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `contactId`, `businessId`, plus custom-field keys. Unknown field or operator is rejected by search (422). Groups may nest. Do not combine `listIds` with a `graph` filter.

listIds.description: List ids to scope the search (max 10). Equivalent to one nested `graph` filter (`type=list`, `id` eq or `contains_set`). More than 10 ids, a non-list target, or a second graph scope returns **422** (`error`: `graph_scope_invalid`).

subtaskViewMode.description: How subtasks appear. Allowed: `collapsed` (parents only), `expanded` (parents with embedded `subtasks[]`), `separate` (subtasks as their own records with `parentTaskId` / `parentName`). Requires a Tasks V2 / Kanban location. On any other location this field, or a `parentTaskId` filter, returns **422**. `parentName` and `subtasks` are search-only — Get Task By ID, Get Tasks, and Fetch Tasks By IDs do not populate them. `total` is the hit count after filters and access scope (post-RBAC). Page with `searchAfter` until it is null.

If it is already an additional member of the destination, `DELETE /projects/lists/{listId}/tasks/{taskId}` on that list, then call Move Task. There is no separate error code for the two causes.

actions.description:
Apply a watermark to an image using either a specific template ID or by resolving the template bound to a specific connected account.

If the same watermark + image combination has been processed before, the response returns immediately with `status: completed` and the output URL in `message`. Otherwise, processing is queued and the response returns `status: pending` with a `progressId`.

**Rate limits:** This endpoint may be rate-limited to prevent abuse. To resolve a template dynamically at publish time, pass `accountId` — the endpoint will resolve the template bound to that connected account. Use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint to look up account IDs.

Processing is asynchronous — the response returns a `progressId` that identifies this preview job.

**Document fields:**
- `status`: 'pending' | 'processing' | 'completed' | 'failed'
- `outputMediaUrl`: string, available when `status` is `completed`
- `errorMessage`: string, available when `status` is `failed`

templateId.description: Template ID to apply. Required if `accountId` is not provided.

accountId.description: Connected account ID — the endpoint will resolve the template bound to this account. Required if `templateId` is not provided. Use the [Get Accounts](./get-account) endpoint to look up account IDs.

inputMediaUrl.description: Input media URL (either video or image)

postId.description: Optional post ID to associate the watermark output with

watermarkId.description: Optional cache key to fetch a previously-generated watermark result

updatePost.description: Whether to update or create the linked post after watermarking

actions.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 3: Connect the Account

This is the final step in the OAuth flow. After retrieving available accounts (Step 2), use this endpoint to connect the selected account to your location.

### OAuth Flow Summary

1. **Start OAuth** → User authenticates with platform
2. **Get Accounts** → Retrieved available pages/channels
3. **Attach Account** (this endpoint) → Connect the selected account

### Request Body

The accepted fields depend on the `platform` path parameter — pick the matching schema in the request body below. Most platforms take the `originId`, `name` and optional `avatar` of the account you selected in Step 2; Google Business Profile takes the full `location` and `account` objects.

> `tiktok-business` accounts are connected through the TikTok Business flow, not this endpoint.

### After Connection

Once connected, the account will appear in your location's connected accounts and can be used for social media posting.
